findings.finding: The GHCR mirror package cannot be created, linked or made public by any job in this change, and the spec's own example depends on it; the implement App also cannot delete a GHCR package version.
findings.answer: The planner opened dispatch://INFRA-567/ask/1a22b043 before drafting; it is answered, make it public. Task B4 confirms an anonymous pull before the cutover lands, and the risk list names the credentials fallback if it is still private.

findings.finding: A mirror written by every pull-request run contradicts the repository's own rule that a trusted attested build must not read a registry path a branch run can write (GHSA-f2v9-hprr-32q3).
findings.answer: The design no longer claims to close the write path: ci.yaml's worker-image job already holds packages: write on a pull request. Every consuming reference is a digest, the two interpolating FROMs included, so no push changes the bytes a build reads. Recorded as departure 8 for the architect.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 1: each fetch 'comes from a source this repository controls or pins, or survives a failure of its third-party source'.
specDepartures.plan: The Go class is delivered under the survives clause alone. GOPROXY becomes https://proxy.golang.org|direct, which falls through on any error; vendoring, the only design meeting the controls clause, is declined.
specDepartures.evidence: Measured in the issue pod with Go 1.27.1: go work vendor at the repository root writes 113 MB in 8,932 files, and in packages/envoy/infra 153 MB in 10,164 files; go mod vendor refuses in workspace mode, so it is two trees. With the root tree, GOPROXY=off go vet -tags e2e ./... in packages/daemon succeeds offline. Against one measured proxy fault in 108 re-run job attempts over 7 days, and 266 MB cloned into every Legion issue pod and the repository cache pod with every bump by hand, since .github/dependabot.yml registers only github-actions.

acceptance: Acceptance 1 for the Go class is met by the survives clause and not by the controls clause.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 1, the same three clauses, for the npm tarball fault of catalog row 64.
specDepartures.plan: The npm class is delivered under the pins clause alone. bun.lock carries a sha512- integrity hash per package and every install is --frozen-lockfile; only the one unlocked install, bun add -g @colbymchenry/codegraph, changes.
specDepartures.evidence: There is no .npmrc and no root bunfig.toml, so every tarball comes from registry.npmjs.org; nothing short of new registry infrastructure or a committed dependency tree makes that fetch survive npmjs.org. The plan's own negative control for it, the worker-image build with registry.npmjs.org unreachable, fails on purpose and is reported.

acceptance: Acceptance 1 for the npm class is met by the pins clause and not by the survives clause; the worker image's frozen install still fetches from registry.npmjs.org.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 1: 'with no retry loop that hides a fault of the repository's own'.
specDepartures.plan: Both image-pull retry loops are deleted, in .github/actions/pull-test-images/action.yml and the hand-written copy in ci.yaml's dispatch job, and that job's pull is folded into the composite action. The pre-pull itself stays.
specDepartures.evidence: Both loops retry a third-party fetch today, which the clause does not name; after the cutover they would retry a ghcr.io fetch, which is this repository's own source. The spec's words order no deletion, so the plan records it rather than assuming it.

outcome.scope: Two retry loops are removed and one duplicated pull step is folded into the composite action.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 3: 'the pull request corrects the README and code-comment prose that describes the files it changes'.
specDepartures.plan: Two docs/solutions pages are retired and replaced, and .dispatch/architecture/release-engineering.md is edited in the same review.
specDepartures.evidence: docs/solutions/github/an-unknown-blob-from-mirror-gcr-io-...-INFRA-303.md and a-ci-red-in-initialize-containers-with-toomanyrequests-...-LEGION-632.md prescribe the re-run this change removes, so leaving them would leave an instruction that defeats acceptance 2. release-engineering.md's front matter claims .github/workflows and .github/scripts, and skill://dispatch requires the code and the architecture document to change in one review.

outcome.scope: Acceptance 3's prose scope grows to two solution documents and one architecture document.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 1 gives 'a copy of each test image in ghcr.io under this repository, pulled by digest' as an example only.
specDepartures.plan: Four new permanent files: .github/ci-images.yaml, .github/scripts/check-ci-images.sh with its test, .github/actions/install-crane and .github/workflows/mirror-images.yaml.
specDepartures.evidence: The mapping from an upstream reference to a mirror tag exists nowhere today, and the drift this change creates, a digest written in ten places and a tag that could move in GHCR, is what a program can check easily. STRATEGY.md's ladder puts a programmatic gate at exactly that case.

outcome.scope: The change adds one data file, one gate script with its test, one composite action and one workflow.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 2: 'In the 7 days after the merge, no job is re-run after a registry, proxy or package-fetch failure; the pull request states the count before and after'.
specDepartures.plan: The pull request states the before-count, the window, the command and the method's three properties. The after-count over the 7 days is the implementer's production check after the close, written into the pull request's Production: line.
specDepartures.evidence: A pull request merges before the 7 days after its own merge exist. dispatch://INFRA-522's retro used the same shape, 'After 7 days, measure.py over the runs on main must ...', and the pending: line for an unfinished window was approved on dispatch://INFRA-588/ask/907faca4.

acceptance: Acceptance 2's after-count is proven by the production check after the close, not in the pull request body.

specDepartures.spec: The spec says nothing about who may write the mirror package; the repository's own rule, in packages/envoy/AGENTS.md and docs/solutions/envoy/ghcr-docker-multiarch-ci.md, forbids a trusted attested build from reading a registry path a branch run can write.
specDepartures.plan: The defence is the digest, not the write path. Every consuming reference names a sha256: digest, the worker image's own FROM lines included, and the two FROMs that interpolate a version today become digests; gate check 2 keeps that true.
specDepartures.evidence: ci.yaml's worker-image job runs on a pull request and grants packages: write so worker-image.yaml can push the head's sha- tag, so a branch run already writes ghcr.io; the rule itself names 'a dispatch of an edited branch copy' as an untrusted writer. The rule protects a tag a cache reads, whose bytes a later push replaces; no push can change the bytes under a digest. The architect must accept this reading, since the rule is written as a rule about the path.
